description: Africana Studies is an interdisciplinary field that investigates the histories, cultures, and intellectual traditions of African peoples and their descendants throughout the world. The department's courses offer a comprehensive examination of African, Afro-American, and Afro-Caribbean societies and cultures. Faculty expertise spans the humanities and social sciences, providing students with a broad and rigorous understanding of the African diaspora. The program is designed to develop students' analytical skills, critical thinking, and capacity for independent research. Graduates are prepared for a wide range of careers in education, public service, law, journalism, and international affairs, as well as for further graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies

description: The Department of American Studies enables students to explore the history, culture, and society of the United States. Its interdisciplinary approach draws upon methods and theories from the fields of history, literature, art history, music, film, performance studies, anthropology, sociology, political science, and philosophy. The department offers a wide range of courses on such topics as race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, law and public policy, urban studies, popular culture, visual culture, environmental studies, and transnational American studies. Students acquire an understanding of the complex forces that have shaped the United States and its place in the world.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies

description: The Department of Anthropology provides a broad introduction to the study of humankind. It covers the major subfields of anthropology: socio-cultural anthropology, archaeology, and biological anthropology, as well as linguistic anthropology. The department’s geographic strengths are in New York City and the Caribbean; Mesoamerica and South America; Western Europe; the Middle East; Southeast Asia; and Sub-Saharan Africa. The undergraduate program includes courses on methods, theory, and specific topics within the subfields, as well as opportunities for fieldwork and study abroad. All students majoring in anthropology are required to take an introductory course, ANTH-UA 1, Introduction to Anthropology, and to take at least one course in each of the four subfields to ensure a broad foundation in the discipline. Anthropology majors are encouraged to develop their interests in consultation with faculty advisers.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology

description: The joint major in Anthropology and Classical Civilization combines the study of the ancient world through the evidence of texts and material culture with a broader and more comparative perspective on human societies, past and present. Students apply methods and theories from both disciplines to understand ancient societies, while also gaining a strong foundation in contemporary anthropological thought and its application to diverse cultural contexts.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology and Classical Civilization

description: The Departments of Anthropology and Linguistics offer a joint major in anthropology and linguistics, leading to a BA degree. The joint major is intended for students interested in language as a cultural, social, cognitive, and biological phenomenon, and in the ways in which human beings use language to create and understand their world. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in both disciplines, emphasizing the interconnections between them. Students are introduced to the theoretical and methodological approaches of anthropology and linguistics, with a particular focus on areas where the two fields intersect, such as linguistic anthropology, sociolinguistics, and cognitive linguistics. The program prepares students for graduate study in anthropology, linguistics, or related interdisciplinary fields, as well as for careers requiring strong analytical, communication, and cross-cultural understanding skills.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology and Linguistics

description: The BA in Art History offers students a comprehensive introduction to the history of art from antiquity to the present day and across global geographies. It provides a foundation in art historical methods, preparing students to critically analyze artworks and to understand the historical, social, and theoretical contexts in which art is produced and perceived. Students develop visual literacy and critical thinking skills, becoming proficient in research, writing, and analytical reasoning through engagement with diverse artistic traditions. The curriculum is designed to foster a deep appreciation for the role of art in human culture, equipping students with the intellectual tools for advanced study in the field or for careers in museums, galleries, cultural heritage, publishing, and other arts-related professions.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Art History

description: The joint major in Art History and Classics is an interdisciplinary program designed for students who wish to combine a strong background in art history with a thorough knowledge of the languages and cultures of the classical world. It is intended for students who wish to pursue a rigorous course of study that combines work in two related disciplines. It offers students an opportunity to gain an understanding of the visual arts of the ancient world in their broader cultural and historical contexts, and to develop critical skills in the analysis of art, texts, and material culture. The program provides a solid foundation for further study in either art history or classics, as well as for careers in museums, galleries, cultural institutions, and related fields. For additional information about the undergraduate curriculum in Classics, consult the Department of Classics website. For additional information about the undergraduate curriculum in Art History, consult the Department of Art History website.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Art History and Classics

description: The Department of Social and Cultural Analysis (SCA) offers an undergraduate major in Asian/Pacific/American Studies that introduces students to the histories, cultures, and societies of Asians and Pacific Islanders in the Americas. As an interdisciplinary field, Asian/Pacific/American Studies critically examines the formation and transformation of Asian/Pacific/American identities, communities, and experiences. The major offers a framework to explore topics such as transnational migration, empire and colonialism, race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, labor and capital, arts and literature, and social justice. Students develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills to engage with complex social and political issues related to Asian/Pacific/Americans and global connections.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Asian/Pacific/American Studies

description: Biochemistry is an interdisciplinary major that combines chemistry and biology. This program is suitable for students interested in the chemical basis of biological phenomena, including areas such as molecular biology, genetics, and cell biology. The B.A. in Biochemistry offers a rigorous course of study in biochemistry with enough flexibility for students to explore other interests or pursue a minor in another area. Students who complete the B.A. in Biochemistry are well-prepared for entry into graduate programs in biochemistry and other health-related fields, as well as medical school or careers in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries. The program is offered jointly by the Department of Biology and the Department of Chemistry. Students must declare the major with both departments.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry

description: The Department of Biology offers two distinct undergraduate majors leading to either a Bachelor of Arts (BA) or a Bachelor of Science (BS) degree. Although students in both programs take common introductory courses, the two majors differ considerably in their specific requirements, objectives, and pedagogical approaches. The BA in Biology is designed for students who are interested in gaining a broad understanding of the biological sciences within a liberal arts education. This degree is particularly suitable for pre-professional students interested in medicine, dentistry, public health, law, and business, as well as students preparing for careers in science writing, secondary education, or government science policy. It also serves as excellent preparation for graduate study in several fields of biology. Students complete a core curriculum consisting of an introductory sequence in biology, chemistry, organic chemistry, physics, and mathematics. They also complete a selection of advanced electives in areas such as genetics, cell biology, neurobiology, ecology, and evolution. Students are encouraged to participate in research with faculty members and to take advantage of opportunities for study abroad.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Biology

description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Biology is a rigorous science major for students who wish to pursue a career in basic or applied research in academia or industry, or to pursue further study in biology at the graduate level. Students complete a total of 15 courses for the major: 10 courses in Biology, 2 courses in Chemistry (General and Organic), 2 courses in Mathematics, and 1 course in Physics.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Biology

description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) program in chemistry is designed for students who wish to gain a broad background in chemistry, but who may not necessarily intend to pursue chemistry as a career. It provides a less intensive alternative to the BS degree and can be readily combined with other fields of study in the humanities, social sciences, or arts. The BA is highly recommended for pre-health students and those interested in careers such as science journalism, secondary school teaching, or business.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry

description: The B.S. program, certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS), is designed for students who intend to pursue graduate work in chemistry or a chemistry-related field, or who plan to enter professions such as medicine, dentistry, or veterinary medicine where a strong background in chemistry is essential.
Accreditation status: Certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS)
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry

description: The undergraduate program in Cinema Studies at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts offers a rigorous academic approach to the history, theory, and aesthetics of film, television, and new media. Students gain a deep understanding of moving images as complex cultural artifacts, exploring their evolution from early cinema to contemporary digital forms. Our curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, analytical writing, and interdisciplinary perspectives. Students will engage with diverse cinematic traditions, explore the social, political, and economic contexts of media production and reception, and develop sophisticated skills in analyzing visual narratives, sound design, and screen theory. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in film criticism, programming, archives, festivals, and further graduate study in media studies, communication, and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Cinema Studies

description: The Department of Classics offers programs in Classical Civilization (BA, minor), Greek (minor), and Latin (minor). Its courses introduce students to the language, literature, philosophy, religion, art, and archaeology of the Greek and Roman world, and to its reception in later cultures. The Classical Civilization program trains students in the history, literature, philosophy, and art of ancient Greece and Rome, as well as in their broader social and cultural contexts. It is ideal for students who wish to immerse themselves in the world of classical antiquity without focusing on the study of ancient languages.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Civilization

description: The Department of Classics offers undergraduate majors in Classics and in Ancient Studies, as well as a minor in Classical Civilization. Courses cover Greek and Latin languages and literatures (epic, tragedy, comedy, lyric, history, philosophy, rhetoric, satire, novels), as well as Greek and Roman history, archaeology, law, art, myth, and religion. The Classics BA major focuses on the languages and literatures of ancient Greece and Rome. Students who pursue this major typically intend to continue their study of classical antiquity at the graduate level.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Classics

description: Comparative literature is the study of literature across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries. It is, by definition, an interdisciplinary field, drawing on courses in national literature departments (English, French, Spanish and Portuguese, Italian, German, Slavic, Middle Eastern, East Asian, and Classics), cinema studies, critical theory, philosophy, history, and the social sciences. The undergraduate major in comparative literature (B.A.) offers students the opportunity to study literary works from different cultures and epochs, to examine theoretical problems, and to develop critical perspectives on cultural production within a global context. The program encourages students to develop their own critical approaches to literary and cultural texts through the intensive study of literary history and theory and the comparative analysis of literary texts. It also provides students with the methodological and theoretical tools necessary for graduate study in comparative literature or related fields. Students are required to take courses in at least two different languages and literatures (including English) and to engage with a variety of theoretical and historical approaches. They are also encouraged to study abroad and to take advantage of the many opportunities available in New York City for the study of global cultures.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature

description: The BA in Computer Science is offered by the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at NYU. The program offers a broad education in computer science and also prepares students for careers in software development and for graduate study in computer science. The BA is designed to provide students with maximum flexibility. It has the fewest required courses of any of our undergraduate majors, allowing students to take a large number of elective courses or even pursue a double major.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science

description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BS CS) program at NYU Tandon School of Engineering provides students with an education in the fundamental principles and practices of computer science, equipping them with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills needed to design, develop, and analyze complex computational systems. Our curriculum covers a broad range of topics, including algorithms, data structures, programming languages, operating systems, computer architecture, and software engineering. We emphasize hands-on experience through labs, projects, and research opportunities, preparing students for successful careers in diverse areas such as software development, data science, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and more. Graduates are also well-prepared for advanced studies in computer science and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

description: The BA in Data Science is a liberal arts degree that introduces students to the foundations of data science from the perspectives of mathematics, computer science, statistics, and domain-specific applications, while providing a broad education in the liberal arts. Students are expected to learn how to: Formulate and solve problems related to data science using a combination of mathematical, computational, and statistical tools; Critically evaluate the quality and reliability of data from various sources; Design and implement algorithms and models for data analysis and prediction; Communicate effectively about data-driven insights to diverse audiences; Understand the ethical implications of data collection, analysis, and use; Apply data science methods to problems in a liberal arts discipline. The degree is suitable for students who wish to pursue careers that leverage data science in areas such as social science, humanities, public policy, business, and communications, as well as those who plan to pursue graduate studies in data science or related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Data Science

description: Dramatic Literature, Theatre History, and Cinema is an interdepartmental program administered by the Department of English and the Department of Cinema Studies. The curriculum, which leads to the BA degree, encompasses a wide range of courses, from dramatic literature through theatre history, criticism, and theory to the study of cinema as an art form. Students learn to analyze theatrical and cinematic texts, performance, and theory; to research and write about theatre and cinema; and to engage with the historical and theoretical developments of both art forms. The major provides a strong foundation for graduate study in theatre, film, or related humanities fields, as well as for careers in arts administration, criticism, programming, curatorship, and education.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Dramatic Literature, Theatre History, and Cinema

description: The Department of East Asian Studies offers students a comprehensive interdisciplinary approach to the cultures, histories, and societies of East Asia, covering China, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam. The BA program provides a strong foundation in a regional language and allows students to explore diverse topics through courses in anthropology, art history, cinema studies, history, linguistics, literature, music, politics, religion, and sociology. Students develop critical analytical skills and a deep appreciation for the complexities of East Asian civilizations, preparing them for careers in international relations, education, business, journalism, and further academic study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies

description: Economics is the study of how societies cope with scarcity. The Department of Economics at NYU offers a wide range of courses in economic theory, empirical methods, and various applied fields. The faculty includes leaders in fields such as econometrics, microeconomic theory, macroeconomic theory, public finance, development economics, international economics, and industrial organization. Many of our faculty also have active appointments or affiliations with other schools within NYU (Stern, Wagner, Law School) as well as the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and the National Bureau of Economic Research. The Department offers a BA and a Minor in economics. Upon graduation, students will be able to: 1. Demonstrate a basic knowledge of fundamental economic theories, models, and concepts. 2. Formulate and evaluate economic arguments. 3. Apply empirical techniques to analyze economic data. 4. Communicate economic ideas effectively in both written and oral form. 5. Demonstrate an awareness of the global and ethical dimensions of economic issues.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Economics

description:
The BA in Economics and Computer Science is a joint program offered by the Department of Economics and the Department of Computer Science. This interdepartmental major has been designed to provide a framework for the serious study of the theoretical and practical connections between economics and computer science.

As technology increasingly changes the way people interact with markets and each other, a strong background in both disciplines will prove extremely valuable for employment in a wide range of fields, including finance, banking, consulting, big data analysis, and entrepreneurship. Students take required courses in both departments and are expected to develop strong analytical and quantitative skills.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Computer Science

description: This combined major is designed for students who want a rigorous, quantitative approach to economics. Students complete requirements for both economics and mathematics, taking courses from both departments. The major allows students to apply mathematical reasoning to economic analysis. It is designed to expose students to the theoretical and empirical tools needed for a broad range of career paths, including graduate study in economics, finance, law, or business.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Mathematics
Bachelor of Science in Engineering

description: The Department of English offers a program in English and American literature leading to the Bachelor of Arts degree. The department’s courses help students to develop their skills in reading, writing, and critical argument; to explore major literary works, periods, genres, and traditions in English and American literature; to situate literature within larger cultural and historical contexts; and to encounter literary forms and critical methods beyond the Anglo-American tradition. The department expects students to combine a broad understanding of literary history with a deep engagement with particular texts and problems.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in English

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences to examine the complex relationship between humans and the natural world. Students learn to critically analyze environmental challenges, develop effective solutions, and understand the ethical and political dimensions of environmental issues. The curriculum emphasizes research, data analysis, and communication skills, preparing students for careers in environmental policy, advocacy, sustainability, resource management, and further academic pursuits.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies

description: European and Mediterranean Studies, also known as EMS, is a vibrant and interdisciplinary program that brings together faculty and students from a wide range of departments and disciplines from across NYU to study the cultural, historical, political, and social issues of Europe and the Mediterranean Basin from ancient to contemporary times. The program is committed to a transnational and interdisciplinary approach, with an emphasis on the Mediterranean as a key site of interaction among diverse peoples, cultures, and religions across North Africa, the Middle East, and Southern Europe. EMS majors are encouraged to engage with global issues and critical debates from a trans-regional and comparative perspective. The program offers students the opportunity to learn about the complexities of Europe and the Mediterranean, a region that is a cradle of civilizations and a key site for the historical and contemporary making of our interconnected world.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in European and Mediterranean Studies
Bachelor of Arts in French

description: The B.A. program in French and Linguistics is designed for students who are fascinated by language and wish to combine a deep knowledge of the structure of French with a broader understanding of general linguistic theory and analysis. The major provides a solid foundation for those students who plan to continue in graduate study in either French or linguistics, as well as for those who intend to pursue careers in fields such as translation, foreign service, government, international business, and teaching. It is particularly well-suited for students who plan on a career involving a specific area of applied linguistics, such as speech processing, computational linguistics, or language acquisition.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in French and Linguistics

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Sexuality Studies provides students with the critical tools to analyze how gender and sexuality shape human experience and social organization across diverse cultures and historical periods. The program introduces students to key theoretical frameworks from the humanities and social sciences to examine topics such as identity formation, power dynamics, social justice movements, cultural representations, and global inequalities. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, research skills, and an understanding of the complex intersections of gender, sexuality, race, class, and and nation. Graduates are prepared for a wide range of careers including activism, education, public policy, journalism, nonprofit management, and further graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Sexuality Studies

description: The Department of German offers a major in German, which provides students with thorough training in German language, literature, and culture. Courses cover a wide range of topics, from medieval literature and philosophy to contemporary film and visual culture. The curriculum is designed to help students develop strong analytical and communication skills, as well as a deep understanding of German-speaking cultures and their global impact. The program encourages interdisciplinary study and offers opportunities for study abroad.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in German

description: The German and Linguistics major is an interdisciplinary program combining a thorough grounding in German language, literature, and culture with a critical engagement with linguistic theory. It offers students the opportunity to combine the study of German with the scientific analysis of language, providing a strong foundation for a wide range of careers including those in education, international relations, communications, translation, and interpretation, as well as for further graduate study in German, linguistics, comparative literature, or related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in German and Linguistics

description: The joint major in Global Public Health/History (BA) gives students a unique lens through which to examine health, disease, and medicine in the context of history. This program enables students to understand the historical dimensions of local and global health issues while developing the research and analytical tools needed to pursue careers related to public health, history, journalism, law, and government. Students will complete courses in both the Department of History and the School of Global Public Health, gaining knowledge and skills in both disciplines.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Global Public Health

description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Global Public Health: Nutrition and Dietetics is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for careers promoting health and preventing disease in diverse communities worldwide. Students learn to address critical global public health issues, including food insecurity, malnutrition, and chronic diseases, through a nutrition lens. This program combines foundational knowledge in public health with in-depth study of nutrition science, food systems, and dietetics practice. Graduates will be equipped to work in various settings, including government agencies, non-governmental organizations, healthcare institutions, and research organizations, both domestically and internationally. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practices, cultural competency, and ethical considerations in public health nutrition.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Global Public Health

description: The Department of Hebrew and Judaic Studies offers a major in Hebrew and Judaic Studies. This major is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of Jewish civilization from antiquity to the present. Students explore the history, religions, literatures, languages, and cultures of the Jewish people. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, drawing on a variety of fields such as history, religious studies, literature, philosophy, and political science. Students develop critical thinking skills, research abilities, and a nuanced perspective on complex historical and cultural phenomena.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Hebrew and Judaic Studies

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Hellenic Studies trains students in the language, literature, history, and culture of the Greek-speaking world, from antiquity to the present. The program is specifically designed to encourage students to pursue their interests in a particular period of Hellenic culture (ancient, Byzantine/medieval, or modern) while also providing them with a broad understanding of the entire sweep of Hellenic civilization. Students take a combination of language and cultural courses. They may apply to spend a semester or year at NYU Athens, which provides an invaluable opportunity to immerse themselves in Greek life and culture.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Hellenic Studies

description: Students declaring a major in Italian Studies will pursue a degree that focuses on the language, literature, and culture of Italy from the Middle Ages to the present day. Students will attain an advanced proficiency in the Italian language, and acquire a thorough knowledge of Italy’s intellectual and cultural heritage through courses in literature, film, history, art history, and cultural studies. The department also offers opportunities for studying abroad through NYU Florence (Villa La Pietra), and offers an Honors Program to qualified students.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies

description: The undergraduate Irish Studies program offers students the opportunity to earn a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Irish Studies or a minor in Irish Studies. Rooted in the humanities and social sciences, the program focuses on the study of Ireland, its diaspora, and its global impact through an interdisciplinary curriculum. It explores history, literature, music, politics, language, and the social sciences related to Ireland and the Irish. Students will develop a critical understanding of the forces that have shaped Irish society, culture, and politics, both historically and in the contemporary world. The program also encourages students to engage with the vibrant Irish community in New York City and offers opportunities for study abroad in Ireland.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Irish Studies

description: The Bachelor of Arts in journalism program integrates the study of liberal arts with training in the practice and principles of journalism, including reporting, writing, editing, and research techniques. Students learn to critically analyze news and information, investigate complex issues, and produce compelling stories across various media platforms. The curriculum emphasizes ethical considerations, the impact of technology on journalism, and the role of journalism in a democratic society. Graduates are prepared for careers in journalism and related fields, as well as for further study in graduate school.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism

description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguists examine such questions as: What is the structure of language? How is language related to the mind and brain? How is language related to society? How do children acquire language? How do languages change? What are the common properties of all human languages and how do languages differ? The major in linguistics is an excellent preparation for graduate work in linguistics and for careers in fields such as speech technology, language education, law, medicine, speech pathology, and international affairs. It is often taken as a double major with computer science, psychology, philosophy, or a foreign language.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics

description: The Department of Mathematics offers three different undergraduate degrees: the B.A. in Mathematics, the B.S. in Mathematics, and the B.S. in Mathematics with a Concentration in Data Science. The B.A. in Mathematics is designed for students who desire a strong foundation in the traditional core areas of mathematics, including algebra, analysis, and geometry, but also wish to pursue significant study in other disciplines. It is particularly suitable for students planning careers in areas such as law, medicine, business, or journalism, where analytical skills are highly valued but extensive graduate study in mathematics is not typically required. The B.A. provides an excellent foundation for interdisciplinary study and double majors.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics

description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematics prepares students for graduate study in mathematics or related fields, or for professional careers in industry, government, or education. Students pursuing the B.S. in Mathematics complete a robust course of study that builds foundational knowledge in calculus, linear algebra, and differential equations, and allows them to delve deeper into advanced mathematical concepts and applications. The program provides a flexible curriculum, enabling students to customize their coursework to align with their specific interests and career aspirations. Our students gain strong analytical and problem-solving skills, which are highly valued in diverse professional settings. A Bachelor of Science degree is also an excellent foundation for graduate study in mathematics or related fields such as physics, engineering, or computer science.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics and Computer Science is a joint program offered by the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Computer Science. The program is an attractive option for students interested in a liberal arts education that combines training in mathematical reasoning with the theoretical and practical foundations of computer science. The curriculum emphasizes fundamental concepts in both disciplines and prepares students for a variety of careers or for graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics and Computer Science

description: The Medieval and Renaissance Studies interdisciplinary major provides students with a broad humanistic education in the art, literature, history, music, philosophy, religion, and languages of medieval and early modern Europe and the Mediterranean. Students will explore the history and culture of these periods through a choice of areas of study and a wide variety of courses, while acquiring strong analytical and communication skills applicable to any career.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Medieval and Renaissance Studies

description: The Middle Eastern Studies major offers an interdisciplinary approach to the diverse areas of study that comprise the Middle East and its diasporas. This major is for students with an interest in the history, politics, religion, culture, and society of the Middle East, as well as developing linguistic fluency in the region’s languages. Students are encouraged to study abroad in the region through NYU’s Global Network University. As such, students pursuing the Middle Eastern Studies major will become experts in the contemporary Middle East through a comprehensive curriculum and language instruction.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Middle Eastern Studies

description: The BA in Music is a flexible course of study, allowing students to explore music through a variety of academic perspectives while maintaining the opportunity to double major or minor in another subject. Students are introduced to the field of music in both its theoretical and historical dimensions, and can then pursue more specialized interests in areas such as performance, music technology, composition, jazz studies, global music, and early music. The BA can also provide a strong foundation for continued study in music at the graduate level.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Music

description: The Neural Science program at NYU Shanghai introduces students to the structure and function of the nervous system. Neural Science is a multidisciplinary field with roots in biology, psychology, chemistry, computer science, and physics. Students completing the Neural Science major are well prepared for careers in research, medicine, public health, and biotechnology. Graduates are also well-prepared for graduate school, medical school, or other health-related professional schools.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Neural Science

description: The Department of Philosophy at NYU is ranked among the top philosophy departments in the English-speaking world. The philosophy major combines breadth of study across the main branches of philosophy (history of philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, aesthetics, political philosophy, and logic) with opportunities for specialized study in the areas of students’ particular interests. The major requirements ensure that students receive a solid grounding in the discipline while also having considerable flexibility to pursue topics or approaches that resonate with them. Many philosophy majors pursue double majors in other fields within the humanities, social sciences, or sciences. Because philosophy develops skills in critical analysis, argumentative writing, and abstract thought, it is excellent preparation for careers in law, public policy, medicine, journalism, and more. A major in philosophy is also often pursued by students who plan to continue their philosophical studies at the graduate level.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy

description: This program provides a strong background in physics and mathematics within a flexible framework, suitable for students interested in a broad liberal arts education, or in careers that require quantitative and problem-solving skills, or in pursuing further study in areas such as law, medicine, finance, or business. It also provides a solid foundation for those intending to pursue graduate studies in fields such as applied physics, geophysics, astronomy, or oceanography, but not typically physics itself. Students who plan to apply to graduate school in physics should pursue the B.S. in Physics (described separately).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Physics

description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Physics is intended for students who wish to pursue graduate work in physics or who plan to seek employment in physics-related fields. This major provides a thorough grounding in the fundamentals of physics and prepares students for a variety of careers.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Physics

description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Politics provides students with a comprehensive understanding of political institutions, behavior, and theory, both in the United States and around the world. The curriculum introduces students to the major subfields of the discipline—American politics, comparative politics, international relations, and political theory—and trains them in the methodological approaches employed in contemporary political science. Through rigorous coursework and research opportunities, students develop strong analytical, research, and communication skills, preparing them for careers in government, law, journalism, non-profit organizations, and further graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Politics

description: The Department of Psychology offers a variety of courses that address fundamental questions about human behavior and thought. The undergraduate program introduces students to the theories and methods of contemporary psychology and to the major findings in the field. Students may pursue a general psychology major, complete the honors program, or declare a joint major with other departments.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology

description: The BA in public policy, offered jointly by the Wilf Family Department of Politics and the Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service, provides a rigorous interdisciplinary course of study for undergraduates interested in careers in public service. The major, which focuses on the analysis and evaluation of public policies and the policy-making process, examines the economic, political, and social forces that shape policy choices. Students develop skills in research, data analysis, and program evaluation. The major offers a foundation for further graduate study in public policy, law, and other professional fields, or for entry-level positions in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy

description: The Department of Religious Studies offers students an opportunity to study the phenomena and varieties of religion in a broad range of its historical and contemporary manifestations across the globe. Students learn to critically examine and analyze religious traditions, their sacred texts, beliefs, practices, institutions, and their impacts on cultures and societies. The program addresses the theoretical and methodological issues involved in the academic study of religion from interdisciplinary perspectives. Students develop a critical understanding of the role religion plays in human experience, both historically and in contemporary society. The Religious Studies major provides a strong liberal arts education and equips students with valuable analytical, research, and communication skills applicable to diverse careers.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies

description: The major in Romance Languages allows students to pursue the study of at least three languages and cultures from the Romance group. Students may choose any three of the following: French, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish. The program is specifically designed to allow students to combine a broad interest in several Romance languages and cultures with the study of common linguistic and literary elements.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Romance Languages

description: The major in Russian and Slavic studies provides an opportunity to study a broad range of subjects pertaining to the literatures, cultures, and societies of Russia and Eastern Europe. Students develop advanced proficiency in the Russian language and choose electives in topics such as literature, history, art, and politics of Russia and Eastern Europe. The department also encourages students to undertake study abroad in Russia or other countries of the region.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Russian and Slavic Studies

description: The Department of Social and Cultural Analysis offers an interdisciplinary undergraduate major that addresses the theoretical and methodological challenges involved in studying the social and cultural aspects of human experience. It is designed for students interested in developing critical perspectives on the historical and contemporary forces that shape human societies, cultures, and individuals across local, national, and transnational contexts. Students are encouraged to develop their own analytical questions through engagement with different theoretical frameworks and methodologies from the fields of anthropology, history, political science, sociology, media studies, ethnic studies, and gender studies. The major also provides students with a strong foundation in research methods and analytical skills, which are essential for graduate study and careers in a variety of fields, including law, public policy, journalism, education, and social justice.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Cultural Analysis

description: Sociology (B.A.) is the scientific study of human social relationships and institutions. The undergraduate curriculum introduces students to the major theoretical and methodological traditions of the discipline and their application to a wide range of substantive topics. The department offers courses in such areas as social inequality, race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, crime and justice, urban sociology, organizations, politics and social movements, culture, health, family, and globalization. Through their coursework, students develop the analytical, research, and communication skills necessary to understand and address complex social issues.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology

description: Develop advanced proficiency in Spanish through rigorous linguistic, literary, and cultural studies. Gain a deep understanding of linguistic theories and methods, with a particular focus on the Spanish language. Analyze the structure and function of Spanish from phonetic, phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic perspectives. Explore the sociolinguistics of Spanish, including dialectal variation, language contact, and language attitudes. Critically engage with literary and cultural texts in Spanish, interpreting their linguistic and cultural significance. Conduct independent research in Spanish linguistics or literary/cultural studies, applying appropriate methodologies and theoretical frameworks. Communicate effectively in Spanish, both orally and in writing, demonstrating nuanced understanding of linguistic and cultural contexts.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish and Linguistics

description: Students of the Spanish and Portuguese major acquire a deep understanding of the languages and cultures of the Spanish and Portuguese-speaking worlds. Through the interdisciplinary study of literature, film, visual arts, music, history, and current events, students hone their critical thinking and analytical skills. The major prepares students for graduate study, as well as for careers in education, diplomacy, international business, translation, law, and other fields that require advanced cross-cultural understanding and linguistic proficiency.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish and Portuguese

description: The Urban Design and Architecture Studies major provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the city, its architectural and urban history, present form, and future design. Students learn to analyze cities through the lenses of history, theory, and design, drawing on a wide range of analytical and representational techniques. They develop skills in critical thinking, research, and communication, preparing them for careers in urban planning, architectural design, historic preservation, real estate, and public policy, as well as for graduate study in related fields. The curriculum includes courses in urban history, architectural history, design studios, and fieldwork opportunities.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Design and Architecture Studies

description: Urban Studies and History is an interdisciplinary major offered jointly by the Department of History and the Gallatin School of Individualized Study. This major explores the history and development of cities, their social, economic, political, and cultural formations, and their representation in various forms of media.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies

description: As a dental hygienist, you’re an integral member of the dental care team. The dental hygienist provides clinical, educational, and therapeutic services that help people maintain optimal oral health. The Associate in Applied Science (AAS) in Dental Hygiene program at NYU College of Dentistry prepares you to deliver these services in a variety of health care settings.
Accreditation status: The dental hygiene program is accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA) of the American Dental Association (ADA).
Program name: Associate in Applied Science in Dental Hygiene
